brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A base with removable bins for small parts
requirements.evidence: Three base pieces (piece full at 0,0 and 0,-1; half-s at 0,1). Two removable 3-compartment bins (bin hex-bin-full-div3) sit in the full bases at (0,-1) and (0,0), each dropping into its cell.
drawer:0#0,1#cut (classic north-style drawer) on the cut face of the half-s base at (0,1).
handle:0,0,0;top sits on the top cover of the (0,0) base, with its inserts; check_build meshClash clear.
Only a joint bolt locks the bases together. capOpenFaces was refused with a MESH_CLASH against the drawer runner, so the open side faces were left uncapped. The build is not fully closed.
The configurator has no part-type check for electronics; the bins are generic. No props or labels were added.

requirements.requirement: Material suitability (durability, ESD safety, portability weight)
requirements.evidence: The configurator does not check materials, weight, or static safety; these depend on the print material chosen.

finish.summary: Built a small portable organizer: three hex base pieces, two removable 3-compartment bins, one drawer on the half base, and a carry handle on the top cover. Final check is meshClash clear with one joint bolt. Caps on the open faces were blocked by a drawer-runner clash, so those faces remain open. Material, ESD and weight requirements cannot be checked here.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
